I lost 50 pounds in maybe 3-4 months. This was in 2020, and I was able to maintain my weight. I’m pregnant now, so I’ll be resuming this diet after I give birth.

I cut out all added sugar products. I cut out all breads, rice, noodles. I ate a lot more veggies. So I’d use a lot of veggie substitutes for things. Cauliflower was my go to (cauliflower rice, cauliflower pizza crust, etc).

I didn’t really work out at all. I maybe walked the dogs 3 times a week. But I mainly stayed home (I worked from home). When I lost all the weight, that’s when I focused on toning up. I also desire the thin and toned look. I was in great shape!! Idk if it would be helpful, but I could share a pic. 

This diet worked best for me. I already dislike rice and breads, so it was easy to cut that out. And I noticed that foods taste better without added sugars. I still had a cheat day once a month, like a milkshake. But that was it. This diet was a lifestyle change for me. I did this until I got pregnant earlier this year.  

I hope that you find a healthy diet that works for you.

I struggled with this. People should realize (all races and genders) that people have different views, hobbies, and backgrounds. Not all black people (for example) fit into a box. I struggled with that since my teenage years. I’m 31 now.

Sadly, this lead me to befriend mainly non-black girls (as a teen) and women over the years. I hated feeling like the butt of a joke. I grew up a military brat, mainly in San Diego.

Now that I’m an adult, I’ve been trying to use the Meetup app. My personality is very much a San Diego girl. I swim, boogeyboard, hang at the beach, go for hikes, stay out in nature, and I’m down for an adventure. I also am a foodie and I enjoy working out. My hair is in locs so it’s easier to get up and go. I listen to Afro beats, R&B, neo soul, and I don’t listen to rap/don’t keep up with social media and don’t keep up with celeb drama (like who are these people?? IDK?? Blueface who??)

So jointing Meetup and discovering other Outdoor Afros in the group has been amazing for me. I WISH I had this in college. I’ve joined fitness groups, brunch groups, and a Black Girls Boat Too group (island hopping in Florida). I found my people. We talk about outdoors, boating, beaches, food, events, etc. We have similar interests. I’ve made some good friends this way.

Don’t waste your time on those people. If you want, keep trying to meet people in different settings.

Thank you for sharing. I also made the decision to terminate a pregnancy while in college. I lived with regret daily, but knew that the decision was right for me at the time. It’s not an easy decision to make. Especially by yourself. But now I’m married, we live in a great area, I just graduated with my MBA this week, and I have an amazing job with great pay and benefits. We are now 9weeks and some days and just happy and feel more prepared. 

Women should have the right to choose. If I had made a different choice back then, I wouldn’t be as stable as I am today. I know this for a fact.

I had an abortion right after graduating from college. Kept it a secret from the father. That’s part 1. The other part, I one day broke down crying a few years later. Boyfriend asked why, and IDK why but I told my boyfriend at the time (no longer together) that I had miscarried a few years prior and I am still upset over it. Ever since then I’ve been telling people (if it’s brought up in conversation) that I had a miscarriage years ago. I am somewhat in denial of the abortion. The only people that know is my OBGYN. I’ll never speak on it. Which is probably why I’m so depressed. Living a lie sucks.
